case.summary: Verdict: legitimate at probability 0.08, pattern none. The $35.66 online purchase (txn 3526826, product code C) was flagged by the real-time model at 0.76, but case memory scored it at cms_p 0.0448 (history family) — far below the fraud band — and the amount sat inside the card's normal baseline (median $59.08). The candidate device "Windows | NULL | chrome 66.0 | NULL" is New but generic (266 cards, not strong), so it carries no shared-origin weight; no card-testing chain, no under-$500 burst, and no other online activity in the surrounding window corroborated fraud, so no episode was built and exposure is $0.00. We asked for customer validation because this was a single-signal risk-score alert with a New device (R1), and the assumed reply was a confirmation that the cardholder recognized the new device and the charge (customer family), which settled the case under R3. Given the card's three prior confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-1475, CC-3216, CC-4294 — account_takeover and card_not_present_new_device patterns), an analyst could reasonably have read this the other way as an early-stage repeat of the CC-3216 new-device fraud shape, but the low cms_p, in-baseline amount, and absence of any corroborating chain member favored the legitimate reading. Recommended route: auto — CREATE_CASE (record kept), ALLOW_TRANSACTION, CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, no approval beyond auto required.
